notes: Service tokens exactly as they are printed on a label, per carrier. This is a
third vocabulary: it is neither the carrier API's service code nor a
CarrierService.service_code. DHL eCommerce prints GRD for the product its own API
calls GND; a FedEx label prints 'FedEx Ground' where the catalog says FEDEX_GROUND.
A token is matched against a whole label field, case-insensitively, never as a
substring of one. Substring matching lets a shorter service name swallow a longer
one -- GROUND would match 'FedEx Ground Economy', which is not FedEx Ground but
FedEx's USPS-last-mile service. A field with no exact entry falls through.
Carrier keys are matched through CarrierAlias::lookupKey against the canonical
carrier name, so a postage source's own spelling resolves through aliases first.
Every entry here is transcribed from a label we hold, and the token is the entire
field as printed. Do not add a token from a carrier's documentation without a label
that prints it -- what a carrier calls a service and what it prints routinely
differ. See issue 14 for the evidence still to be gathered.

dhl express.observed_on: The DHL sample label Shopify returned for a dhl_express:P test purchase on the development store, 2026-09-17 -- a MyDHL API certified test document (SPC Test shipper, waybill 96 3812 1732, stamped SAMPLE), not a label generated for the parcel. It has a text layer and prints the product as a whole field beside WPX, DHL's code for the same product. Whether a live label prints the identical field is unconfirmed; rung 3 answers this carrier from the selection first, so this token only matters for an auto purchase.
